Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. Responsible for directing and managing assigned engineering projects from conception to completion, tracking and assuring project costs are within scope and on schedule.

Our client, an international law firm, is seeking a Director of Technology Infrastructure & Engineering to join their team!.

We are seeking an executive-level Director of Technology Infrastructure & Engineering
to own the overall strategy, continuous modernization, and operational stability of the firm’s global technology foundation.

Align departmental objectives with broader business priorities, establishing rigorous service-level agreements (SLAs), operational governance, and risk mitigation strategies.

Manage corporate email delivery, secure messaging gateways, and productivity suite integrations.

Supervise core network services, load balancing, virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), and database administration functions.
Manage departmental CapEx/OpEx budgets, contract negotiations, and strategic relationships with major technology vendors and global platform providers.

Experience: 10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience directing complex, multi-site infrastructure and engineering teams.
Industry Experience: Strong preference for candidates coming out of prestigious professional services environments (e.g., global law firms, management consulting, investment banking, or financial services).

Executive Presence: Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into strategic dialogue for non-technical senior executives and business stakeholders.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or an equivalent technical field required.

Strong leadership, stakeholder management, and communication skills.

Define the technical roadmap for cloud platforms, DevOps, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and AI assisted engineering tools

Experience implementing M Files or a comparable document management system
Experience working within a regulated, document intensive, or professional services environment

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Brief Description

POSITION SUMMARY:
The Director, Security Architecture and Engineering, is responsible for the strategy and oversight of the Information Security Engineering and Architecture within FPI (Financial Partners, Inc). The Director of Security Architecture & Engineering leads the development and execution of FPI’s enterprise security architecture strategy, ensuring robust protection of systems, data, and infrastructure. This role provides technical leadership, integrating security best practices across cloud and on-prem environments while aligning with regulatory and industry standards. Collaborating with senior leadership and IT teams, the Director drives innovation, risk mitigation, and the implementation of scalable, resilient security solutions.

Duties And Responsibilities

Develop and maintain a Security Architecture and Engineering framework for a large financial services technology provider.
Identify security design gaps in existing and proposed architectures and implement solutions that ensure alignment with industry standards, technology strategies, and organizational goals.
Ensure that all project rollouts meet stringent security standards and are effectively integrated with existing applications and systems, particularly within cloud ecosystems.
Develop information security policies, practices, and recommendations for technology enhancements as necessary to reflect changing technology trends and security initiatives.
Develop and enhance architecture and engineering standards to be used within FPI and partner associations.
Provide guidance and work with stakeholders on implementing security best practices and Azure-specific security configurations.
Contribute to evaluating and recommending security products and services, reporting directly to the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), who retains final decision-making authority.
Stay informed about emerging threats and vulnerabilities, particularly those targeting cloud platforms, and proactively communicate risks and ensure appropriate teams are engaged to implement mitigation strategies.
Foster close collaboration with cross-departmental business teams to champion and drive support for and adherence to security initiatives.
Responsible for organizing and leading mock security events across the company and client base to test and enhance organizational preparedness and response capabilities.
Perform security risk assessment, testing, and monitoring of security programs and policies and coordinate with the Head of Internal Audit to ensure that the target results meet the expectations of our regulators and customers.

We're partnering with Quant
, a global leader in digital transformation and technology solutions, seeking a Head of Platform Reliability

Head of Platform Reliability

The Clearing House's On-Chain Money Initiative will let US financial institutions clear and settle tokenized deposits on chain, connected to the RTP® and CHIPS® networks. Quant powers it, and we need someone to own its reliability ahead of an expected launch in the first half of 2027.
That means the full production environment (OP Stack, a private Besu L1, Paladin nodes, the Overledger Gateway, the Settlement Bridge and the Audit Store), the service levels and error-budget policy, and the authority to stop a release when the budget is spent. You would also build and lead the team that runs it, on a three-shift rotation you design and take part in yourself.
Chain platforms fail differently: state is expensive, restarts are not a strategy, and much of what looks like infrastructure is protocol behavior. If that sounds interesting rather than daunting, we should talk.

You will need

To have led site reliability or production engineering somewhere failure had consequences.
To have run error budgets in practice: used one to stop a release, and defended the call.
Honest experience of 24x7, multi-shift coverage. What burns people out, what does not, and the difference between a rotation on paper and one people can live with.
Kubernetes, Terraform, and an observability stack you have actually debugged rather than configured.

Useful, not essential

Blockchain nodes in production, particularly Besu or another Ethereum client.
Banking, payments, or somewhere else an auditor asked you to prove something.

There is more to this than we can put in an advertisement. If it sounds like your kind of problem, apply and we will tell you the rest on a call.

About Quant

Almost all the money in the economy is commercial bank money, and almost none of it moves on chain. Quant is a leading provider of programmable money infrastructure, and our technology changes that: it lets banks issue, move and settle tokenized deposits around the clock, automatically and securely, while staying connected to the systems they already run on. It is already deployed in regulated environments with central and commercial banks in the UK and around the world, including work on the digital pound and the digital euro.

The Clearing House, whose networks clear and settle more than $2 trillion a day, has now selected Quant to power its On-Chain Money Initiative: a new interoperable payments network that will let financial institutions of all sizes clear and settle tokenized deposits, with connectivity to the RTP® and CHIPS® networks. Our technology provides the network's interoperability, orchestration and transaction-management layer, enabling payments that settle immediately and transactions that trigger automatically once agreed conditions are met.

Through our Tokenized Deposits-as-a-Service solution, banks of any size can join without building new infrastructure themselves. The network is expected to become available to participating institutions in the first half of 2027, with use cases across corporate treasury, liquidity management, cross-border payments and digital asset settlement. We are building the New York team that will run it.
